api_change: SchedulerWakePort::deliver(&mut self, prepared: Self::Prepared, committed: SchedulerWakeCommit<'_>) -> FabricPortResult<()>. SchedulerWakeCommit borrows actual owner scheduler/capacity fields and includes occurrence: usize. Activation, command, choose, concrete registration and simulation drain APIs are unchanged.
observation_logic: Owner constructs SchedulerWakeCommit directly from &self.capacity.scheduler and &self.capacity.state after publishing scheduler/capacity/Ready state; the production change is only borrowed references and an index, with no new allocation.

Behavioral test observer captures those actual borrowed fields at entry to deliver, before invoking the concrete ThreadSchedulerWakeAdapter or SimulationSchedulerWakeAdapter. It never reacquires the owner mutex to obtain the boundary observation.

Live boundary packets are consumed by the actual parked receiving worker after concrete thread delivery. Simulation observations are paired with indices independently drained from the actual simulation adapter.

The shared receiver predicate checks the boundary occurrence/key is Ready, actual active/Ready counts equal capacity usage, and generation/profile/release facts agree. Normal consumption also compares the captured boundary state with final owner state.
wrong_order_control: receiving_boundary_rejects_real_delivery_before_publication covers both real concrete backends and both Running Yield / Blocked Wake. It previews the authoritative admitted command, prepares the actual target, then deliberately delivers using the same owner's real unpublished Running/Blocked fields through a cfg(test) disjoint-borrow accessor. The normal receiver predicate must return false for that concrete delivery; owner state must remain exactly unchanged. The subsequent normal owning command must pass the identical receiver predicate.
denied_delivery_accounting: Each non-Woken/non-Yielded command and every choose synchronously checks cumulative prepare and deliver counts against consumed delivery sequences.
Accepted effects must be received before any new checkpoint control wake. Consumption then checkpoints, detecting additional/unaccounted preparation or delivery.

Live checkpoints are FIFO behind preceding real-delivery boundary packets. Receiver acknowledgement includes the exact checkpoint sequence and total consumed delivery count; an unexpected Delivery before the acknowledgement fails immediately.

A confirmation packet is sent only after the explicit control unpark returns. Receiver waits for that confirmation, drains any pending control permit with zero-duration park_timeout without drawing any absence inference, acknowledges, and re-enters park before processing later commands.
Successful Drop checkpoints before Stop; it cannot silently discard a final erroneous delivery. Panic teardown merely terminates the already-failed test without a second panic.
Timeouts now only bound failure to receive required positive progress/checkpoint acknowledgements, never infer absence of an effect.
migration: Both concrete delivery implementations, owner callsite, behavioral observer and committed-uncertainty fault regression use the new delivery argument. Source inventory found no old deliver signatures or DENIED_OBSERVATION/RecvTimeoutError::Timeout absence checks in fabric_time.
verification: No builds, tests, lint, formatter, lifecycle or git commands executed. Parent still owns formatting and the first post-edit acceptance campaign; no execution/pass claim is made.
